The Death of the Continuous Derivative

In legacy physics, velocity is a smooth, continuous slide across a void, defined by the derivative v = \frac{dx}{dt}span_8span_8. Because it assumes \Delta t can become infinitely small, it assumes motion is frictionlessspan_9span_9.

In the active field, motion is not a slide; it is a localized sequence of discrete actualizationsspan_10span_10. A state change must be handed off from one adjacent node to the nextspan_11span_11. The causal math replaces the continuous derivative with the discrete step function of Propagation Frictionspan_12span_12. Every time a relational state advances by one Planck length (delta X), it incurs a baseline thermodynamic cost (\mu)span_13span_13.
The continuous path integral is replaced by a discrete summation of network routing hopsspan_14span_14: E_{dissipated} = \sum_{n=1}^{N} \mu \cdot delta X_n
